title: Cost Anomaly Detection

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.14 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.14 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:billing` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.14_cost_anomaly_detection_14"
| sort -_time
description: Unexpected spend spikes indicate runaway resources, cryptomining attacks, or misconfigured services. Catching anomalies early saves money.
value: Detecting cost anomaly detection early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable CUR reports to S3. Ingest via Splunk_TA_aws (billing input). Calculate daily baselines per service. Alert when daily spend exceeds 2 standard deviations from the 30-day average.
visualization: Line chart (daily spend with threshold), Table (anomalous services), Stacked area (spend by service).
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable: this cost or advisory feed is not a CIM data model. Use the search in Step 2 on the billing or support API data you ingest.
knownFalsePositives: Month-end or quarter spikes, RIs, savings plans, and new services the statistical model has not seen yet.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:billing`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable CUR reports to S3. Ingest via Splunk_TA_aws (billing input). Calculate daily baselines per service. Alert when daily spend exceeds 2 standard deviations from the 30-day average.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.14_cost_anomaly_detection_14"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:billing` in `index=aws` to detect cost anomaly detection. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_14_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (daily spend with threshold), Table (anomalous services), Stacked area (spend by service)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cost anomaly detection so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
